title: A calmer sign-up for a challenger bank
summary: Lumen was losing one in three applicants before they finished onboarding. We rebuilt the flow around one question per screen and cut the median time to account by half.
results: -52%:Time to open an account|+31%:Completed applications|98:Lighthouse performance score
testimonialQuote: They treated onboarding as a product, not a form. Completion went up in the first week and support tickets fell.
content:
## The challenge

Lumen's application asked for everything up front: identity, income, employment and a proof-of-address upload on a single long page. Mobile users, who made up most of the traffic, abandoned it at the document step.

## What we did

We mapped every field to the regulatory requirement behind it, dropped the ones that could be collected after approval, and split the rest into a short sequence with clear progress. Copy for errors and edge cases was rewritten with the compliance team so it stayed accurate and readable.

- One question per screen, saved as you go
- Document upload deferred until after a soft credit check
- Editable content in Payload so compliance can update wording without a release

## The outcome

The new flow shipped behind a flag and ran against the old one for three weeks before we switched fully. Median time to open an account halved and completed applications rose by almost a third.

title: A patient portal people actually open
summary: Fernwood's portal was a login wall in front of a PDF list. We turned it into a booking-first dashboard that works on a five-year-old phone.
testimonialQuote: Our receptionists finally have time for the people standing in front of them.
content:
## The challenge

Patients could view results online but not book, reschedule or message the practice. Most still phoned, and the reception team spent their day on calls that a good interface could have handled.

## What we did

We interviewed reception staff and a dozen patients, then rebuilt the portal around the three jobs people actually came to do: book, reschedule, and read a result. Accessibility was a hard requirement from the first wireframe, tested with a screen reader and at 200% zoom.

## The outcome

Bookings moved online at a rate the practice had not expected, and call volume dropped enough that opening hours for phone support could be reduced without complaints.

title: Headless storefront for an outdoor retailer
summary: Oakline's monolithic shop platform was slow and hard to change. A headless rebuild made category pages instant and gave merchandisers control over content.
testimonialQuote: We went from waiting on developers to launching a campaign page in an afternoon.
content:
## The challenge

Category pages took over four seconds to become usable on mobile, and every merchandising change needed a developer. Peak-season traffic regularly pushed the old platform to its limits.

## What we did

We separated content from commerce: Payload holds editorial content and landing pages, the shop platform stays the source of truth for stock and price, and Next.js stitches them together with incremental static regeneration so pages are fast and still fresh.

- Incremental regeneration for category and product pages
- Structured data and clean URL migration to protect existing rankings
- Editor-friendly campaign pages built from reusable blocks

## The outcome

Category pages became near-instant, mobile conversion climbed, and the site held steady through the next seasonal peak with no scaling incidents.

title: One place for a school's students, parents and staff
summary: Meridian ran its communications through five tools. We consolidated them into one site with role-based news, timetables and a calendar parents can subscribe to.
testimonialQuote: Parents told us it was the first time they could find things without ringing the office.
content:
## The challenge

Announcements went out by email, a legacy intranet, two messaging apps and a noticeboard. Information was duplicated, contradicted itself, and reached parents late.

## What we did

We built one publishing workflow: staff write once in Payload, choose who should see it, and the site handles the rest. Calendar feeds and printable timetables came from the same content, so nothing had to be retyped.

## The outcome

The office now publishes in a single place and the number of "where do I find…" enquiries fell sharply within the first term.

title: A direct-booking site for a boutique hotel group
summary: Saltmarsh relied on booking platforms that took a large cut. A faster, better-written site shifted a meaningful share of reservations to direct.
testimonialQuote: The site finally sounds like our hotels. Guests mention it in their reviews.
content:
## The challenge

The group's own site was a thin brochure that sent visitors to third-party platforms as soon as they showed interest. Photography was heavy and copy was generic.

## What we did

We rewrote every property page around what guests actually ask before booking, rebuilt image handling so galleries load quickly, and put availability search above the fold with a clear price promise.

## The outcome

Direct bookings grew steadily over the following two quarters and the group saw its platform commission bill drop.

title: Making renewable energy tariffs easy to compare
summary: Greenloop's tariff calculator confused visitors and scared off good leads. A plain-language redesign quadrupled completed quotes.
testimonialQuote: Customers now arrive already understanding the tariff, so sales conversations start further along.
content:
## The challenge

The quote calculator asked for a meter reference most people did not have to hand, and results were shown as a wall of unit rates. Visitors left without a clear next step.

## What we did

We replaced the meter reference with a simple estimate based on household size, showed results as a monthly cost with the assumptions visible, and wrote a set of guides in answer to the questions the sales team heard most.

- Estimate-first calculator with editable assumptions
- Guides written with the sales team and published from the CMS
- Structured data for tariffs and FAQs

## The outcome

Completed quotes quadrupled and the guides became a steady source of organic traffic.

title: A property search that respects the reader
summary: Harbor & Vale's listings were buried under filters and pop-ups. A faster search with map and list views brought enquiries up without more ad spend.
testimonialQuote: Agents stopped sending us screenshots of things that were broken. That says it all.
content:
## The challenge

Search pages loaded slowly, filters reset when you navigated back, and a chat pop-up covered the first listing photo on mobile.

## What we did

We moved search state into the URL so every result page is shareable and the back button behaves, added a synchronised map and list view, and removed the pop-up in favour of a persistent enquiry button.

## The outcome

Enquiries per listing view rose steadily and the agents reported fewer support requests about the site.

title: A knowledge base that answers before support does
summary: Corvid's docs lived in three places and nobody trusted them. One searchable knowledge base cut repeat tickets by a third.
testimonialQuote: Support now links to an article instead of typing the same answer for the tenth time.
content:
## The challenge

Product docs sat in a wiki, a help centre and a folder of PDFs. Articles contradicted one another and search returned duplicates.

## What we did

We consolidated the content model into a single collection with versioned drafts, migrated and de-duplicated the archive, and built search that ranks by how often an article actually resolves a ticket.

## The outcome

Repeat tickets fell by a third and the support team gained a reliable source to point customers to.

title: A coffee roaster's subscription, rebuilt for retention
summary: Tidewater's subscribers cancelled because changing a delivery felt risky. Clear controls and honest reminders lifted retention.
testimonialQuote: Letting people skip a delivery without a fuss made them stay longer. Obvious in hindsight.
content:
## The challenge

Subscribers could pause or cancel but not easily skip, swap a bag or change frequency. Most who felt overstocked simply cancelled.

## What we did

We rebuilt the account area around small, reversible actions, added a reminder before each shipment with one-tap skip and swap, and refreshed the brand voice to feel warmer and less transactional.

## The outcome

Cancellations fell noticeably and retention at six months improved.

title: A clinic network's find-a-doctor, done properly
summary: Brightpath's 40 clinic pages were near-duplicates. A structured content model let each location rank for its own neighbourhood.
results: +92%:Local search visits|40:Clinic pages generated from one template
testimonialQuote: Every clinic finally has a page that is accurate and unique. We update it once and it stays right.
content:
## The challenge

Clinic pages were copied from a template with the name changed. Opening hours were wrong on many, and none ranked locally.

## What we did

We modelled clinics, practitioners and services as related collections, so each page pulls accurate details from a single source and adds local context written by the clinic teams.

## The outcome

Local search visits nearly doubled and the operations team no longer chases outdated hours.

title: Quotes in minutes for a specialist insurer
summary: Atlas's broker portal needed a phone call to quote anything unusual. A guided quote tool handled most cases online.
results: 70%:Quotes completed without a call|-2 days:Average time to bind
testimonialQuote: Brokers get an answer while the client is still on the line.
content:
## The challenge

Standard cover could be quoted online, but anything specialist needed an underwriter call and a two-day wait.

## What we did

We worked with underwriters to encode their rules as questions the tool could ask, with clear fallbacks for the cases that still need a human, and gave brokers a saved-quote view they could return to.

## The outcome

Most quotes now complete without a call and the time to bind dropped sharply.

title: A supplier directory for a food producers' co-op
summary: Wildroot's members had no shared showcase. A directory with stories and sourcing details became the co-op's best sales tool.
testimonialQuote: Buyers now come to us having already read the producer's story.
content:
## The challenge

Members were small producers with strong stories and no web presence. Buyers had to be introduced one at a time.

## What we did

We built a directory where each producer can maintain their own profile through a simplified editing view, with sourcing and certification details presented consistently.

## The outcome

Wholesale enquiries increased and the co-op now uses the directory as its main introduction to new buyers.

title: Design system and marketing site for a B2B platform
summary: Kestrel had three visual identities across product and marketing. We unified them into one design system and a site that ships changes weekly.
testimonialQuote: Product and marketing finally look like the same company.
content:
## The challenge

A rebrand had left product, marketing and sales collateral in three different styles, and every new page was a design negotiation.

## What we did

We audited the existing work, defined a small set of tokens and components, and built the marketing site on top of them so new pages could be assembled by the team without a designer in the loop.

## The outcome

Launching a new page went from weeks to days, and customers began commenting on how consistent the company felt.

title: Rebuilding a language school's course finder
summary: Prospective students could not tell which course fit them. A short level check and clearer course pages doubled enquiries.
testimonialQuote: Students now arrive knowing which level they are, which saves everyone time.
content:
## The challenge

Course pages listed hours and prices but did not explain who each course was for. Prospective students guessed, and often guessed wrong.

## What we did

We wrote each course page around the learner it suits, added a brief level check that recommends a starting point, and made timetables filterable by day and evening availability.

## The outcome

Enquiries doubled and the admissions team reported far fewer placement mismatches.
